title.zh: 卷43 列傳第8 河間王弘 楊處綱 楊子崇 觀德王雄
title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 8: He Jian Wanghong, Yang Chugang, Yang Zichong, Guang De, Wang Xiong
title.raw: 卷43 列傳第8 河間王弘 楊處綱 楊子崇 觀德王雄 Volume 43 Biographies 8: He Jian Wanghong, Yang Chugang, Yang Zichong, Guang De, Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 隋書卷四十三列傳第八

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 43, Biographies, Number Eight
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 43, Biographies 8

sentences.zh: 河間王弘

translations.literal: Hejian Wang Hong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, Prince of Hejian

sentences.zh: （子慶）

translations.literal: (His son Qing)
translations.idiomatic: (His son Qing)

sentences.zh: 河間王弘，字辟惡，高祖從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Hejian Wang Hong, styled Bie'e, was a younger male cousin of Emperor Gaozu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, Prince of Hejian, courtesy name Bie'e, was a cousin of Emperor Wen on the paternal line.

sentences.zh: 祖愛敬，早卒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aijing died young.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aijing died at an early age.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，少孤，隨母郭氏養于舅族。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun, orphaned in youth, was raised by his mother Lady Guo among her maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuansun lost his parents in childhood and was brought up by his mother, Lady Guo, among her maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 及武元皇帝與周太祖建義關中，元孫時在鄴下，懼為齊人所誅，因假外家姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuyuan and Zhou's founding emperor raised the banner of righteous rebellion in Guanzhong, Yuansun was then in Ye and, fearing execution by the people of Qi, took his maternal family's surname of Guo as his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuyuan and the Zhou dynastic founder raised their banner in Guanzhong, Yuansun was still in Ye. Fearing the Northern Qi would put him to death, he assumed his maternal clan's surname and became Guo.

sentences.zh: 元孫死，齊為周所並，弘始入關，與高祖相得。

translations.literal: Yuansun died; when Qi was absorbed by Zhou, Hong first entered the passes and found favor with Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuansun died and Qi was overrun by Zhou, Hong finally entered Guanzhong, where he and the future Emperor Wen became close.

sentences.zh: 高祖哀之，為買田宅。

translations.literal: Gaozu took pity on him and purchased fields and a residence for him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his plight, Emperor Wen bought him land and a house.

sentences.zh: 弘性明悟，有文武幹略。

translations.literal: Hong was bright and perceptive by nature, with both civil and military talent and resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was quick-witted by nature and possessed both literary and military ability.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，累遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He often followed on campaigns and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Third Rank Supervisor of the Imperial Retinue with the Opening of an Office.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in several campaigns and rose in stages to the rank of Acting Third Rank Supervisor with the Opening of an Office.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，常置左右，委以心腹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chancellor, he was kept constantly at his side and entrusted as an intimate confidant.
translations.idiomatic: While still serving as chancellor, Yang Jian kept Hong close at hand and treated him as one of his most trusted inner circle.

sentences.zh: 高祖詣周趙王宅，將及於難，弘時立於戶外，以衛高祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu went to the residence of Zhao, Prince of Zhou, and was about to meet with disaster, Hong stood outside the door at the time to guard Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion when Yang Jian visited the residence of Zhao, Prince of Zhou, and nearly came to harm, Hong stood guard outside the door to protect him.

sentences.zh: 尋加上開府，賜爵永康縣公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally given Opening of an Office and granted the title Marquis of Yongkang County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also granted the privilege of opening his own office and given the title Marquis of Yongkang County.

sentences.zh: 及上受禪，拜大將軍，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: When the emperor accepted the abdication, he was appointed Grand General and advanced in rank to Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian ascended the throne, Hong was made Grand General and promoted to Duke of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋贈其父為柱國、尚書令、河間郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his father was posthumously ennobled as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter his late father was posthumously honored as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其年立弘為河間王，拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: That same year Hong was installed as Prince of Hejian and appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hong was created Prince of Hejian and appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，進授柱國。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，以行軍元帥率眾數萬，出靈州道，與虜相遇，戰，大破之，斬數千級。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks were a repeated menace on the frontier; as commander of the field army he led a force of tens of thousands by the Lingzhou route, encountered the barbarians, fought, and utterly defeated them, taking several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were repeatedly raiding the frontier, he served as commander of the field army at the head of tens of thousands of men. Marching out along the Lingzhou route, he met the enemy in battle and routed them, beheading several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賜物二千段，出拜甯州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was granted two thousand bales of goods, was sent out as Director-General of Ning Province, and advanced to First Rank Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded with two thousand bales of textiles, he was appointed Director-General of Ning Province and promoted to First Rank Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 弘在州，治尚清靜，甚有恩惠。

translations.literal: In his province, Hong's governance valued quiet simplicity, and he showed much kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial governor he favored a light, unobtrusive administration and was widely regarded as a benevolent ruler.

sentences.zh: 後數載，征還京師。

translations.literal: Several years later he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜蒲州刺史，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed governor of Pu Prefecture and granted discretion to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was made governor of Pu Prefecture with authority to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 時河東多盜賊，民不得安。

translations.literal: At the time there were many bandits in Hedong, and the people could not live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rampant in Hedong at the time, and the people lived in constant fear.

sentences.zh: 弘奏為盜者百餘人，投之邊裔，州境帖然，號為良吏。

translations.literal: Hong petitioned regarding more than a hundred robbers, exiling them to the frontier regions; the territory of the prefecture became calm, and he was acclaimed as a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Hong identified more than a hundred robbers and had them sent to the frontier. With the territory at peace, he won renown as an outstanding official.

sentences.zh: 每晉王廣入朝，弘輒領揚州總管，及晉王歸籓，弘複還蒲州。

translations.literal: Whenever Prince Jin Guang came to court for an audience, Hong would take charge as Director-General of Yang Province; when the Prince of Jin returned to his fief, Hong would resume his post at Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Prince Guang of Jin visited the capital, Hong would temporarily serve as Director-General of Yang Province; when the prince returned to his fief, Hong would go back to Pu.

sentences.zh: 在官十餘年，風教大洽。

translations.literal: In office for more than ten years, customs and education were thoroughly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade in office, he brought local customs and moral instruction into excellent order.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征還，拜太子太保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Hong was recalled and appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Hong was recalled and made Grand Mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，薨。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，追封郇王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 6 (610), he was posthumously created Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 子慶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qing succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qing inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 慶傾曲，善候時變。

translations.literal: Qing was pliable and adept at reading the changing times.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was pliable by nature and skilled at reading which way the wind was blowing.

sentences.zh: 帝時猜忌骨肉，滕王綸等皆被廢放，唯慶獲全。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was suspicious of his kinsmen; Princes of Teng Lun and others were all deposed and banished, but Qing alone escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew suspicious of his own kin and deposed or banished princes such as Lun of Teng, Qing alone escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 累遷滎陽郡太守，頗有治績。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he became Administrator of Xingyang Commandery and achieved considerable administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to Administrator of Xingyang Commandery, he compiled a solid record of governance.

sentences.zh: 及李密據洛口倉，榮陽諸縣多應密，慶勒兵拒守。

translations.literal: When Li Mi seized the Luokou granary, many counties of Xingyang responded to Mi; Qing mustered troops to resist and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi seized the Luokou Granary and many Xingyang counties rallied to him, Qing raised troops and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 密頻遣攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Mi repeatedly sent forces to attack but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent repeated assaults but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，城中糧盡，兵勢日蹙。

translations.literal: After more than a year, grain in the city was exhausted, and the military situation grew daily more strained.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the city's food ran out and its defensive position grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 密因遺慶書曰：

translations.literal: Mi therefore sent Qing a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi then sent Qing a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 自昏狂嗣位，多曆歲年，剝削生民，塗炭天下。

translations.literal: Since the benighted and mad ruler succeeded to the throne, many years have passed, plundering the living people and scorching the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since that benighted tyrant took the throne, year after year he has stripped the people bare and plunged the land into misery.

sentences.zh: 璿室瑤台之麗，未極驕奢；

translations.literal: The splendor of jade chambers and azure terraces has not yet reached the limit of arrogant extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: The marvels of his jade halls and azure towers scarcely exhaust his arrogance and excess;

sentences.zh: 糟丘酒池之荒，非為淫亂。

translations.literal: The wastefulness of wine pools and meat hills is not merely for the sake of debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: Nor are his meat hills and wine pools simply wanton indulgence—they mark something far worse.

sentences.zh: 今者共舉義旗，勘剪凶虐，八方同德，萬里俱來，莫不期入關以亡秦，爭渡河而滅紂。

translations.literal: Now we jointly raise the banner of righteousness to punish and cut down the cruel and tyrannical; the eight directions share one purpose, and men come from ten thousand li; none fail to aspire to enter the passes as Qin was destroyed, or to cross the river to annihilate Zhou as Shang was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Today we have raised the banner of righteous rebellion to strike down a brutal regime. From every quarter men have rallied, arriving from a thousand miles away, each longing to sweep into Guanzhong as the armies did when they brought down Qin, or to cross the river and topple a tyrant as when Zhou fell to the Zhou founders.

sentences.zh: 東窮海、岱，南洎江、淮，凡厥遺人，承風慕義，唯滎陽一郡，王獨守迷。

translations.literal: East to the sea and Mount Tai, south to the Yangtze and Huai, all the surviving people catch the wind and admire the cause—only in Xingyang Commandery does Your Highness alone stubbornly hold to delusion.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern seas and Mount Tai to the Yangtze and the Huai, every survivor who still breathes has taken up our cause—yet in all this, only Xingyang Commandery, and Your Highness alone, still clings to the doomed order.

sentences.zh: 夫微子紂之元兄，族實為重，項伯籍之季父，戚乃非疏，然猶去朝歌而入周，背西楚而歸漢。

translations.literal: Wei Zi was King Zhou of Shang's elder brother by blood—the kinship was truly weighty; Xiang Bo was Xiang Ji the Overlord of Western Chu's uncle—the affinity was by no means distant—yet they still left Chaoge to enter Zhou and turned their backs on Western Chu to return to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zi was King Zhou of Shang's own elder brother—the tie of blood could scarcely have been closer; Xiang Bo was Xiang Ji of Western Chu's uncle—hardly a distant kinsman—yet both men left Chaoge to join King Wu of Zhou, and turned from Western Chu to serve the Han.

sentences.zh: 豈不眷戀宗祊，留連骨肉，但識寶鼎之將移，知神器之先改。

translations.literal: Was it not that they cherished the ancestral altars and were bound to their flesh and blood? They simply recognized that the precious tripod was about to be transferred and knew that the divine vessel would change hands first.
translations.idiomatic: Did they not love their ancestral altars and feel the pull of kinship? They simply understood that the Mandate was already shifting, and that the throne would soon pass to another house.

sentences.zh: 而王之先代，家住山東，本姓郭氏，乃非楊族。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Highness's forebears dwelt in Shandong; their original surname was Guo—they are not of the Yang clan at all.
translations.idiomatic: Your own ancestors came from the east, bore the surname Guo, and were never truly of the Yang line.

sentences.zh: 止為宿與隋朝先有勳舊，遂得預沾磐石，名在葭莩。

translations.literal: Merely because of longstanding meritorious ties with the Sui dynasty in former days, you were privileged to share in the solidity of bedrock and counted among the closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Only because of old ties of service to the Sui did you come to be treated as one of the dynasty's closest and most trusted kin.

sentences.zh: 婁敬之與漢高，殊非血胤，呂布之于董卓，良異天親，芝焚蕙歎，事不同此。

translations.literal: Lou Jing and Emperor Gaozu of Han were utterly without blood relation; Lü Bu and Dong Zhuo were truly unlike natural kin—the orchid burns while the sweet flag sighs; this matter is not the same as those.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jing stood with Emperor Gaozu of Han though they shared no blood; Lü Bu served Dong Zhuo though heaven had made them no kin. When one orchid withers the others may grieve, but your case is not like that.

sentences.zh: 又王之昏主，心若豺狼，仇忿同胞，有逾沉、閼，惟勇及諒，咸磬甸師，況及族類為非，何能自保！

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Highness's sovereign is a benighted ruler whose heart is like a wolf or jackal; he treats his own brothers with enmity exceeding the parricides Chen and Que; only Yong and Liang met annihilation at the frontier—what fate awaits even your clan when guilt is imputed? How can you preserve yourself!
translations.idiomatic: And consider your sovereign: benighted and wolf-hearted, more savage toward his own brothers than the worst villains of old. Princes Yong and Liang were wiped out to the last man—why would your branch of the family fare any better?

sentences.zh: 為王計者，莫若舉城從義，開門送款，安若太山，高枕而臥，長守富貴，足為美談，乃至子孫，必有餘慶。

translations.literal: For Your Highness's counsel, nothing is better than surrendering the city to join the righteous cause, opening the gates to offer allegiance—you would be secure as Mount Tai, sleeping with head on high pillow, long preserving wealth and honor, ample material for fine story, and even to your descendants there would surely be leftover blessing.
translations.idiomatic: If I may advise Your Highness, your best course is to surrender the city and join our cause—to open the gates and submit. You would be as secure as Mount Tai itself, sleeping at ease while your wealth and rank endure. That would be a tale worth telling, and your descendants would reap the reward.

sentences.zh: 今王世充屢被摧蹙，自救無聊，偷存晷漏，詎能支久？

translations.literal: Now Wang Shichong has repeatedly been driven and pressed; he cannot save himself and lives on stolen moments—how can he hold out long?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong is already battered on every side, barely able to save himself; he lives on borrowed time. How long can he last?

sentences.zh: 段達、韋津，東都自固，何暇圖人？

translations.literal: Duan Da and Wei Jin in the Eastern Capital fortify themselves—what leisure have they to think of others?
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da and Wei Jin are busy holding the Eastern Capital together—they have no time to think of anyone else.

sentences.zh: 世充朝亡，達便夕滅。

translations.literal: If Shichong dies in the morning, Da will perish by evening.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong falls in the morning, Duan Da will be gone by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 又江都荒湎，流宕忘歸，內外崩離，人神怨憤。

translations.literal: Furthermore, at Jiangdu the emperor indulges in wild debauchery, drifting away and forgetting to return; within and without there is collapse and separation, and men and spirits alike seethe with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the emperor at Jiangdu gives himself over to dissipation and shows no sign of returning. Court and country are coming apart, and both men and gods are filled with fury.

sentences.zh: 上江米船，皆被抄截，士卒饑餒，半菽不充，事切析骸，義均煮弩。

translations.literal: Rice ships coming upriver are all intercepted and seized; soldiers hunger and starve, with not even half a portion of beans to fill them—the situation presses toward splitting bones for food; righteousness demands boiling bowstrings for broth.
translations.idiomatic: Grain ships heading upriver are seized before they arrive; the soldiers starve, unable even to fill half their bellies with beans. Men are already reduced to splitting the dead for meat—in spirit no different from boiling a bowstring for soup.

sentences.zh: 舉烽火于驪山，諸侯莫至；

translations.literal: Beacon fires were raised on Mount Li, yet no feudal lords came;
translations.idiomatic: Beacon fires blaze on Mount Li, yet no allies come to the rescue—

sentences.zh: 浮膠船于漢水，還日未期。

translations.literal: while glue boats float on the Han River—the day of return is not yet set.
translations.idiomatic: while the emperor amuses himself with his glued boats on the Han, with no return in sight.

sentences.zh: 王獨守孤城，絕援千里，餱糧之計，僅有月餘，敝卒之多，才盈數百，有何恃賴，欲相拒抗！

translations.literal: Your Highness alone holds a solitary city, with aid cut off a thousand li away; stores of dry provisions will last barely a month or more; worn-out soldiers barely exceed a few hundred—upon what do you rely, that you wish to resist us!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness holds a lone city a thousand li from any help. Your dry rations will last barely a month; your weary troops number only a few hundred at best. What do you have to resist us with?

sentences.zh: 求枯魚於市肆，即事非虛；

translations.literal: To seek dried fish in the marketplace—the matter is no empty figure;
translations.idiomatic: To go to the market for dried fish is no mere figure of speech—

sentences.zh: 因歸雁以運糧，竟知何日。

translations.literal: to rely on returning wild geese to transport grain—who knows what day that might be?
translations.idiomatic: and to hope wild geese might bring your grain, who can say when that would be?

sentences.zh: 然城中豪傑，王之腹心，思殺長吏，將為內啟。

translations.literal: Yet within the city are bold heroes, Your Highness's trusted confidants, who think of killing the chief official and will open from within.
translations.idiomatic: And within your walls are men of spirit among your closest followers, already plotting to slay their superiors and open the gates from inside.

sentences.zh: 正恐禍生匕首，釁發蕭牆，空以七尺之軀，懸賞千金之購，可為寒心，可為酸鼻者也。

translations.literal: One truly fears disaster arising from a dagger, trouble bursting from within the palace walls—you would in vain offer your seven-foot frame with a thousand in gold placed on your head; it is enough to chill the heart and sour the nose.
translations.idiomatic: I fear disaster may come from a dagger at close hand, or rebellion erupt behind your own walls—you would offer up your life while a price of a thousand in gold is put on your head. The thought makes one shudder; it turns the stomach.

sentences.zh: 幸能三思，自求多福。

translations.literal: I hope you will think thrice and seek your own greater blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to weigh this carefully and choose what will bring you fortune.

sentences.zh: 于時江都敗問亦至，慶得書，遂降於密，改姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: At that time news of the Jiangdu defeat also arrived; Qing received the letter and thereupon surrendered to Mi, changing his surname back to Guo.
translations.idiomatic: About then word came of the disaster at Jiangdu. Qing read Li Mi's letter and surrendered to him, reverting to the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 密為王世充所破，複歸東都，更為楊氏，越王侗不之責也。

translations.literal: Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong; Qing returned to the Eastern Capital, again became Yang, and Prince Yue Tong did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong, Qing returned to the Eastern Capital, took the Yang surname once more, and Yang Tong, Prince of Yue, did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 及侗稱制，拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: When Tong assumed the regency, Qing was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong assumed regency, Qing was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 世充將篡，慶首為勸進。

translations.literal: When Shichong was about to usurp, Qing was the first to urge him to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong prepared to seize the throne, Qing was first to urge him on.

sentences.zh: 世充既僭偽號，降爵郇國公，慶複為郭氏。

translations.literal: Once Shichong had presumptuously assumed a dynastic title, Qing's rank was reduced to Duke of Xun, and Qing again became Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong declared himself emperor, Qing was demoted to Duke of Xun and again adopted the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 世充以兄女妻之，署滎州刺史。

translations.literal: Shichong gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage and appointed him governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong married him to his elder brother's daughter and made him governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 及世充將敗，慶欲將其妻同歸長安，其妻謂之曰：「國家以妾奉箕帚於公者，欲以申厚意，結公心耳。

translations.literal: When Shichong was nearing defeat, Qing wished to take his wife with him to Chang'an; his wife said to him: "The state gave me to you as your wife to express deep regard and to win your loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Shichong's defeat drew near, Qing wanted to take his wife with him to Chang'an. She said to him, "The state gave me to you in marriage to show you good faith and win your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今叔父窮迫，家國阽危，而公不顧婚姻，孤負付屬，為全身之計，非妾所能責公也。

translations.literal: Now my uncle is driven to desperation, the state and family are on the brink of peril, yet you disregard our marriage bond and betray the trust placed in you—if this is a plan to preserve yourself, it is not for me to reproach you for it."
translations.idiomatic: Now that my uncle is at the end of his rope and his regime is failing, and you would abandon our marriage to save yourself—I cannot fault you for choosing to survive."

sentences.zh: 妾若至長安，則公家一婢耳，何用妾為！

translations.literal: If I were to reach Chang'an, I would be nothing but a servant in your household—what use would there be in taking me!"
translations.idiomatic: But if I reached Chang'an, I would be nothing but a servant in your house. What purpose would I serve there?"

sentences.zh: 願得送還東都，君之惠也。

translations.literal: I only wish to be sent back to the Eastern Capital—that would be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Let me return to the Eastern Capital—that would be your act of grace."

sentences.zh: 」慶不許。

translations.literal: Qing would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Qing refused.

sentences.zh: 其妻遂沐浴靚妝，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: His wife then bathed, dressed herself beautifully, and died by taking poison.
translations.idiomatic: His wife bathed, dressed herself in her finest clothes, and took poison.

sentences.zh: 慶歸大唐，為宜州刺史、郇國公，複姓楊氏。

translations.literal: Qing returned to the Great Tang, was made governor of Yi Province and Duke of Xun, and again took the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Qing then submitted to the Tang and was appointed governor of Yi Province and Duke of Xun, resuming the surname Yang.

sentences.zh: 其嫡母元太妃，年老，兩目失明，王世充以慶叛己而斬之。

translations.literal: His principal mother, Grand Consort Yuan, was elderly and blind in both eyes; Wang Shichong had her executed because Qing had betrayed him.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Grand Consort Yuan, was elderly and blind in both eyes. Wang Shichong had her executed when Qing defected.

sentences.zh: ○楊處綱

translations.literal: ○ Yang Chugang
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chugang

sentences.zh: 楊處綱，高祖族父也。

translations.literal: Yang Chugang was a senior clansman of Gaozu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chugang was an elder kinsman of Emperor Wen on the Yang clan side.

sentences.zh: 生長北邊，少習騎射。

translations.literal: He grew up on the northern frontier and from youth practiced horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the northern frontier, he trained in riding and archery from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 在周嘗以軍功拜上儀同。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou he was once appointed Senior Acting Associate in Chief of an Office for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou he was promoted to Senior Acting Associate on the strength of his military service.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，贈其父鐘葵為柱國、尚書令、義城縣公，以處綱襲焉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he posthumously ennobled Chugang's father Zhongkui as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Yicheng County; Chugang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, he posthumously honored Chugang's father Zhongkui as Pillar of State, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Yicheng County, and Chugang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 授開府，督武候事。

translations.literal: He was granted Opening of an Office and supervised the affairs of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the privilege of opening his own office and put in charge of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋為太子宗衛率，轉左監門郎將。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Colonel Director of the Heir Apparent's Clan Guard and then transferred to Left Commandant of the Monitoring Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Colonel Director of the crown prince's clan guard, then transferred to Left Commandant of the Monitoring Gate.

sentences.zh: 後數載，起授右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed Right Corps Commander General.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled and appointed Right Corps Commander General.

sentences.zh: 處綱雖無才藝，而性質直，在官強濟，亦為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Although Chugang had no special talent or accomplishment, his nature was straightforward; in office he was forceful and effective, and was likewise praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Chugang had no special gifts, but he was upright by nature and forceful in office, and won respect in his day.

sentences.zh: 尋拜蒲州刺史，吏民悅之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Pu Prefecture, and officials and people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Pu Prefecture, where officials and commoners alike welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 後遷秦州總管，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred as Director-General of Qin Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Director-General of Qin Province, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Respectful (Gong).

sentences.zh: 弟處樂，官至洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chule reached the office of governor of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chule rose to become governor of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反也，朝廷以為有二心，廢錮不齒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, the court believed Chule had divided loyalties; he was deposed, imprisoned, and disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, the court suspected Chule of divided loyalties; he was stripped of rank, imprisoned, and disgraced.

sentences.zh: ○楊子崇

translations.literal: ○ Yang Zichong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zichong

sentences.zh: 楊子崇，高祖族弟也。

translations.literal: Yang Zichong was a clansman and younger cousin of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zichong was a younger clansman-cousin of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 父盆生，贈荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Pensheng was posthumously made governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pensheng was posthumously honored as governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 子崇少好學，涉獵書記，有風儀，愛賢好士。

translations.literal: Zichong from youth loved learning, ranged widely through books and records, had dignified bearing, and loved worthies and honored gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong loved study from childhood, read widely, carried himself with dignity, and delighted in talented men.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜儀同，以車騎將軍恆典宿衛。

translations.literal: In the early Kaihuang period he was appointed Acting Associate and regularly served as Palace Guard with the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made Acting Associate and regularly performed palace guard duty as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後為司門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Director of the Department of Gatekeepers.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Director of the Department of Gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，累遷候衛將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, through repeated promotion he became General of the Guarding Retinue, but was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, he rose to General of the Guarding Retinue but was dismissed when implicated in an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複令檢校將軍事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to serve provisionally as a general on military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was again entrusted with provisional command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 從帝幸汾陽宮，子崇知突厥必為寇患，屢請早還京師，帝不納。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to the Fenyang Palace, Zichong knew the Turks would surely become a raiding menace and repeatedly petitioned for an early return to the capital; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the emperor to the Fenyang Palace, Zichong was convinced the Turks would soon raid the frontier and repeatedly urged an early return to the capital, but the emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 尋有雁門之圍。

translations.literal: Before long there was the siege at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came the siege at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，帝怒之曰：「子崇怯軟，妄有陳請，驚動我眾心，不可居爪牙之寄。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the emperor angrily said: "Zichong is cowardly and soft, recklessly making petitions and disturbing the hearts of my troops—he cannot hold the trust of a close military post."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, the emperor raged at him: "Zichong is cowardly and weak. His ill-timed warnings have unsettled the army. He is unfit to hold a commander's post."

sentences.zh: 」出為離石郡太守，治有能名。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Lishi Commandery and gained a reputation for capable governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Administrator of Lishi Commandery, where he nevertheless earned a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥屢寇邊塞，胡賊劉六兒複擁眾劫掠郡境，子崇上表請兵鎮遏。

translations.literal: From this time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier passes, and Hu bandit Liu Liu'er again gathered followers to plunder the commandery territory; Zichong submitted a memorial requesting troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Turks raided the frontier repeatedly, and the rebel Liu Liu'er gathered forces to pillage the commandery. Zichong petitioned for troops to restore order.

sentences.zh: 帝複大怒，下書令子崇巡行長城。

translations.literal: The emperor again flew into a rage and issued an edict ordering Zichong to inspect the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor erupted in anger again and ordered Zichong to make a patrol inspection of the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 子崇出百餘裡，四面路絕，不得進而歸。

translations.literal: Zichong went out more than a hundred li; roads were cut off on all sides, and he could not advance and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong marched out more than a hundred li, but every route was blocked and he was forced to turn back.

sentences.zh: 時百姓饑饉，相聚為盜，子崇前後捕斬數千人。

translations.literal: At the time the common people were famine-stricken and gathered to become bandits; Zichong in succession captured and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With famine driving people to banditry, Zichong captured and executed several thousand in the course of his duties.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，朔方梁師都、馬邑劉武周等各稱兵作亂，郡中諸胡複相嘯聚。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Liang Shidu of Shuofang, Liu Wuzhou of Mayi, and others each raised troops in rebellion; the various Hu in the commandery again rallied one another in assembly.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Liang Shidu in Shuofang and Liu Wuzhou in Mayi each rose in arms, and the non-Han peoples of the commandery likewise began gathering in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 子崇患之，言欲朝集，遂與心腹數百人自孟門關將還京師。

translations.literal: Distressed by this, Zichong said he wished to attend a court assembly and thereupon, with several hundred trusted followers, set out from Mengmen Pass intending to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by the growing chaos, Zichong announced that he would go to court and, with several hundred trusted men, set out from Mengmen Pass toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 輜重半濟，遇河西諸縣各殺長吏，叛歸師都，道路隔絕，子崇退歸離石。

translations.literal: When the baggage train was half across, they encountered the various counties west of the river each killing their chief officials and defecting to Shidu; the roads were cut off, and Zichong withdrew back to Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Their baggage train was still half across the river when word came that the counties west of the Yellow River had killed their magistrates and joined Liang Shidu. With the roads cut off, Zichong retreated to Lishi.

sentences.zh: 所將左右，既聞太原有兵起，不復入城，遂各叛去。

translations.literal: The followers he had brought, having heard that troops had risen at Taiyuan, would no longer enter the city and thereupon each deserted and left.
translations.idiomatic: His men, hearing that an army had risen at Taiyuan, refused to re-enter the city and deserted one by one.

sentences.zh: 子崇悉收叛者父兄斬之。

translations.literal: Zichong entirely apprehended the fathers and elder brothers of the deserters and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong rounded up the fathers and elder brothers of the deserters and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 後數日，義兵夜至城下，城中豪傑複出應之。

translations.literal: Several days later, righteous-army troops arrived at the city by night, and bold heroes within the city again came out to answer them.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later rebel troops appeared outside the walls by night, and prominent locals inside the city opened the gates to join them.

sentences.zh: 城陷，子崇為仇家所殺。

translations.literal: The city fell; Zichong was killed by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell, and Zichong was killed by men who bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: ○觀德王雄弟達

translations.literal: ○ Guande Wang Xiong's younger brother Da
translations.idiomatic: Guande Prince Xiong — his younger brother Da

sentences.zh: 觀德王雄，初名惠，高祖族子也。

translations.literal: Guande Wang Xiong, originally named Hui, was a clansman's son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Guande Prince Xiong, originally named Hui, was a clansman-son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 父紹，仕周，曆八州刺史、儻城縣公，賜姓叱呂引氏。

translations.literal: His father Shao served under Zhou, successively governing eight provinces as governor, and was Duke of Tangcheng County, granted the surname Chilüyin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao had served the Northern Zhou as governor of eight provinces in succession, held the title Duke of Tangcheng County, and been granted the surname Chilüyin.

sentences.zh: 雄美姿儀，有器度，雍容閒雅，進止可觀。

translations.literal: Xiong had handsome bearing, possessed capacity and magnanimity, was composed and refined in leisure, and his advances and halts were admirable to behold.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was handsome and dignified, with a calm, elegant bearing and a presence that commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為太子司旅下大夫。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu of Zhou's reign, he served as Junior Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Retinue Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he held the post of Junior Grand Master of the crown prince's retinue protocol.

sentences.zh: 帝幸雲陽宮，衛王直作亂，以其徒襲肅章門，雄逆拒破之。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Yunyang Palace, Prince Wei Zhi raised a rebellion and with his followers attacked the Su Zang Gate; Xiong met them in resistance and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Yunyang Palace, Prince Zhi of Wei rebelled and led his followers in an assault on the Su Zang Gate; Xiong met the attack and routed them.

sentences.zh: 進位上儀同，封武陽縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Acting Associate, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Acting Associate and created Duke of Wuyang County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 累遷右司衛上大夫。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he became Senior Grand Master of the Right Guard Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Senior Grand Master of the Right Guard Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大象中，進爵邗國公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang period he was advanced to Duke of Han State with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he was promoted to Duke of Han with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，雍州牧畢王賢謀作難，雄時為別駕，知其謀，以告高祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chancellor, Bi Wang Xian the Governor of Yong Province plotted rebellion; Xiong was then an assistant administrator, learned of the plot, and reported it to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian served as chancellor, Bi Wang Xian, Governor of Yong Province, plotted rebellion. Xiong, then serving as assistant administrator, discovered the plot and reported it to Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 賢伏誅，以功授柱國、雍州牧，仍領相府虞候。

translations.literal: Xian was executed after confessing guilt; for this merit Xiong was appointed Pillar of State and Governor of Yong Province, and still headed the chancellor's guard patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was executed. For this service Xiong was made Pillar of State and Governor of Yong Province while continuing to command the chancellor's guard patrol.

sentences.zh: 周宣帝葬，備諸王有變，令雄率六千騎送至陵所。

translations.literal: At the burial of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, fearing that the various princes might create trouble, he ordered Xiong to lead six thousand cavalry to escort the procession to the tomb site.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xuan of Zhou's funeral, fearing the princes might cause trouble, the court ordered Xiong to escort the procession to the tomb with six thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was advanced to First Rank Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to First Rank Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，除左衛將軍，兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was made Left Guard General and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Xiong was appointed Left Guard General and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右衛大將軍，參預朝政。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and participated in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and given a voice in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 進封廣平王，食邑五千戶，以邗公別封一子。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping with a fief of five thousand households; one of his sons was separately enfeoffed with the title of Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Prince of Guangping with a fief of five thousand households, and one son was separately given the title Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 雄請封弟士貴，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Xiong requested that his younger brother Shigui be enfeoffed; the court granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong petitioned to have his younger brother Shigui enfeoffed, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 或奏高熲朋黨者，上詰雄於朝。

translations.literal: When someone memorialized that Gao Jiong had formed a clique, the emperor interrogated Xiong in court.
translations.idiomatic: When someone accused Gao Jiong of forming a faction, the emperor questioned Xiong about it at court.

sentences.zh: 雄對曰：「臣忝衛宮闈，朝夕左右，若有朋附，豈容不知！

translations.literal: Xiong replied: "I am honored to guard the inner palace, at the emperor's side morning and night—if there were clique attachment, how could I not know it!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied, "I serve at the emperor's side day and night. If Gao Jiong had gathered a clique, I would surely know of it!

sentences.zh: 至尊欽明睿哲，萬機親覽，熲用心平允，奉法而行。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is discerning, clear, and sagacious, personally reviewing all affairs of state; Jiong's mind is even and fair, and he acts in accordance with law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is wise and personally oversees every matter of state. Gao Jiong is fair-minded and acts strictly according to law.

sentences.zh: 此乃愛憎之理，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: This is simply the logic of favor and hatred—I ask Your Majesty to discern it."
translations.idiomatic: This accusation springs from personal likes and dislikes. I ask Your Majesty to see through it."

sentences.zh: 」高祖深然其言。

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply approved of his words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen found his answer entirely convincing.

sentences.zh: 雄時貴寵，冠絕一時，與高熲、虞慶則、蘇威稱為「四貴」。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong's honor and favor surpassed all others of the age; together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei he was called the "Four Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his career Xiong's favor eclipsed all rivals; together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei he was known as one of the "Four Exalted Ones."

sentences.zh: 雄寬容下士，朝野傾矚。

translations.literal: Xiong was tolerant and deferential toward gentlemen; court and countryside alike looked to him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was gracious toward men of talent, and all eyes in court and country turned toward him.

sentences.zh: 高祖惡其得眾，陰忌之，不欲其典兵馬。

translations.literal: Gaozu disliked his winning the loyalty of the masses and secretly envied him, not wishing him to command troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen resented his popularity and secretly distrusted him; he did not want Xiong in command of military forces.

sentences.zh: 乃下冊書，拜雄為司空，曰：「維開皇九年八月朔壬戌，皇帝若曰：於戲！

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an investiture document appointing Xiong as Minister of Works, saying: "It is the first day renxu of the eighth month of the ninth year of Kaihuang; the emperor says: Alas!"
translations.idiomatic: He therefore issued an investiture edict creating Xiong Minister of Works: "On the first day, renxu, of the eighth month, Kaihuang 9, the emperor speaks: Alas!"

sentences.zh: 惟爾上柱國、左衛大將軍、宗正卿、廣平王，風度寬弘，位望隆顯，爰司禁旅，綿曆十載。

translations.literal: You, First Rank Pillar of State, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Prince of Guangping—your bearing is broad and magnanimous, your rank and repute lofty and illustrious; you have long managed the forbidden troops, continuously for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: You, First Rank Pillar of State, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Prince of Guangping—of generous bearing and illustrious standing, you have commanded the palace guard these ten years past.

sentences.zh: 入當心腹，外任爪牙，驅馳軒陛，勤勞著績。

translations.literal: Within you served as intimate confidant; without you wielded imperial power; you hurried about the palace halls, and your diligent toil has shown merit.
translations.idiomatic: Within you have been the emperor's trusted confidant; without you have wielded the dynasty's authority, serving tirelessly at court with conspicuous merit.

sentences.zh: 念舊庸勳，禮秩加等。

translations.literal: Recalling your old ordinary merit, ceremonial rank is advanced a grade.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of your long and faithful service, your ceremonial rank is hereby raised.

sentences.zh: 公輔之寄，民具爾瞻，宜竭乃誠，副茲名實，是用命爾為司空。

translations.literal: The trust of a state minister—the people all look up to you; you should exhaust your sincerity to match this name and reality; therefore I appoint you Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The burden of a chief minister rests on you, and the people look to you accordingly. Devote yourself fully to the charge. I therefore appoint you Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go—revere this!
translations.idiomatic: Go forth and fulfill this trust!

sentences.zh: 光應寵命，得不慎歟！

translations.literal: To reflect glory upon this favored appointment—can you not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: You have received an honor of the highest kind—act with all due care!

sentences.zh: 」外示優崇，實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Outwardly it showed high esteem; in reality it stripped him of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly it was a mark of highest honor; in fact it removed him from command.

sentences.zh: 雄無職務，乃閉門不通賓客。

translations.literal: Xiong had no official duties and thereupon shut his gate, refusing to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: With no official duties left to him, Xiong shut his gates and refused visitors.

sentences.zh: 尋改封清漳王。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon re-created Prince of Qingzhang.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，高祖曰：「清漳之名，未允聲望。

translations.literal: At the start of Renshou, Gaozu said: "The name Qingzhang does not accord with his reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era Emperor Wen said, "The title Prince of Qingzhang does not match his standing."

sentences.zh: 」命職方進地圖，上指安德郡以示群臣曰：「此號足為名德相稱。

translations.literal: He ordered the Bureau of Garrisons to present a map; pointing to Ande Commandery he showed the officials and said: "This title is fully worthy to match his name and virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the map brought and, pointing to Ande Commandery, showed it to the officials: "This title is worthy of his reputation."

sentences.zh: 」於是改封安德王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was thereupon re-created Prince of Ande.

sentences.zh: 子恭仁，位至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Gongren reached the office of Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongren rose to become Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 恭仁弟綝，性和厚，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Gongren's younger brother Shen was gentle and generous by nature and possessed considerable literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren's younger brother Shen was mild and generous by nature and had some literary talent.

sentences.zh: 曆義州刺史、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Yi Province and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Yi Province and administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 及父薨，起為司隸大夫。

translations.literal: When his father died, he was recalled and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，帝令綝於臨海頓別有所督。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, the emperor ordered Shen to be stationed separately at Linhaidun with special oversight duties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign the emperor assigned Shen separate supervisory duties at Linhaidun.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反也，玄感弟玄縱自帝所逃赴其兄，路逢綝。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Xuangan's younger brother Xuanzong escaped from the emperor's side to join his elder brother and encountered Shen on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Xuangan's brother Xuanzong fled the imperial camp to join him and met Shen on the road.

sentences.zh: 綝避人偶語久之，既別而複相就者數矣。

translations.literal: Shen, avoiding others, spoke briefly with him for a long time; after parting they came together again several times.
translations.idiomatic: Shen spoke with him at length out of others' hearing, parted—and then they came together again, more than once.

sentences.zh: 司隸刺史劉休文奏之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiuwen memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiuwen reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時綝兄吏部侍郎恭仁將兵於外，帝以是寢之，未發其事。

translations.literal: At the time Shen's elder brother Vice Director Gongren was commanding troops outside; the emperor on this account suppressed the matter and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shen's elder brother Gongren was then commanding troops in the field, the emperor set the matter aside and took no action.

sentences.zh: 綝尤懼，發病而卒。

translations.literal: Shen was especially fearful, took ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was terrified; he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 綝弟續，仕至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Shen's younger brother Xu reached the office of Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's younger brother Xu rose to become Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 雄弟達，字士達。

translations.literal: Xiong's younger brother Da, styled Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's younger brother Da, courtesy name Shida.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，有學行。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, with learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 仕周，官至儀同、內史下大夫，遂甯縣男。

translations.literal: Serving under Zhou, he reached the offices of Acting Associate and Junior Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and was Baron of Suining County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou he rose to Acting Associate and Junior Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and held the title Baron of Suining County.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜給事黃門侍郎，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Da was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and promoted to viscount.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾寇邊，詔上柱國元諧為元帥，達為司馬。

translations.literal: At the time the Tuyuhun raided the frontier; an edict appointed First Rank Pillar of State Yuan Xie as commander and Da as chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tuyuhun raided the frontier, Yuan Xie was appointed commander with Da as his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 軍還、兼吏部侍郎，加開府。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was additionally made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Personnel and granted Opening of an Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was additionally made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and granted the privilege of opening his own office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉內史侍郎，出為鄯、鄭、趙三州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: After more than a year he transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and was sent out as governor of the three provinces of Shan, Zheng, and Zhao, all with reputations for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he became Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, then served as governor of Shan, Zheng, and Zhao in succession, earning a reputation for competent administration in each.

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，四海大同，上差品天下牧宰，達為第一，賜雜彩五百段，加以金帶，擢拜工部尚書，加位上開府。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, when the realm under heaven was united, the emperor graded all the prefectural governors of the land; Da ranked first and was granted five hundred bales of mixed colored silks, additionally given a gold belt, promoted to Director of the Department of Public Works, and given the rank of Senior Opening of an Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen and the unification of the realm, the emperor ranked every provincial governor in the land. Da placed first. He was rewarded with five hundred bales of colored silks and a gold belt, promoted to Director of the Ministry of Public Works, and granted the rank of Senior Opening of an Office.

sentences.zh: 達為人弘厚，有局度。

translations.literal: Da as a man was magnanimous and generous, with capacity and breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: Da was openhearted and magnanimous, a man of broad vision and steady judgment.

sentences.zh: 楊素每言曰：「有君子之貌，兼君子之心者，唯楊達耳。

translations.literal: Yang Su often said: "Among those who have both the appearance of a gentleman and the heart of a gentleman, there is only Yang Da."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su often said, "Among those who look the gentleman and are one in spirit, Yang Da is the only example I know."

sentences.zh: 」獻皇后及高祖山陵制度，達並參豫焉。

translations.literal: In the regulations for the tombs of Empress Xian and Gaozu, Da participated in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Da played a part in planning the tomb arrangements for Empress Xian and Emperor Wen alike.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉納言，仍領營東都副監，帝甚信重之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Palace Reporter, still concurrently serving as Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital; the emperor greatly trusted and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Da became Palace Reporter and served concurrently as deputy supervisor of the Eastern Capital project. The emperor trusted and relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，領右武衛將軍，進位左光祿大夫，卒于師，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he commanded as General of the Right Martial Guard, was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died in the army; at the time he was sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he served as General of the Right Martial Guard and was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. He died in camp at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆惜者久之，贈吏部尚書、始安侯。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in regret for a long time and posthumously granted him Director of the Department of State Affairs Personnel and Marquis of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length and posthumously honored him as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Marquis of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Respectful (Gong).

sentences.zh: 贈物三百五十段。

translations.literal: Three hundred fifty bales of goods were granted in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred fifty bales of goods were granted in his honor.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖始遷周鼎，眾心未附，利建同姓，維城宗社，是以河間、觀德，咸啟山河。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: When Gaozu first moved the tripod of Zhou, hearts were not yet attached; enfeoffing those of the same surname to protect the altars of state was advantageous—therefore Hejian and Guande both opened territories across mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When Emperor Wen first seized the Mandate, loyalties were still unsettled. He enfeoffed men of the Yang clan to buttress the throne—thus the princes of Hejian and Guande were both granted domains spanning mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 屬乃葭莩，地非寵逼，故高位厚秩，與時終始。

translations.literal: Their kinship was but as reed and rush roots; their domains were not positions of favor and pressure—therefore high rank and thick stipends lasted with the times from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Being only distant kin and holding no positions that threatened the throne, they enjoyed high rank and generous stipends from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 楊慶二三其德，志在苟生，變本宗如反掌，棄慈母如遺跡，及身而絕，宜其然矣。

translations.literal: Yang Qing wavered in his virtue twofold and threefold, his aim set on saving his own life—changing his original clan as easily as turning over the palm, abandoning his loving mother as if leaving no trace; that his line ended in his own person was fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing was inconstant in his loyalties and cared only to save his own skin—changing his clan as easily as turning his hand, abandoning his stepmother as if she were nothing. That his line ended with him was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 觀王位登臺袞，慶流後嗣，保茲寵祿，實仁厚之所致乎！

translations.literal: Guande's position reached the highest court rank; blessing flowed to his descendants who preserved these favors and stipends—was this not truly the effect of benevolence and generosity!
translations.idiomatic: Guande Prince Xiong rose to the highest honors, and his descendants inherited his rank and favor—is that not the reward of a generous and forbearing nature?
